note: Real PayPal sandbox runs (not agent test rounds). Each links its raw JSON (ids and statuses only, no credentials). Counts are as recorded.

runs.title: The money path, PayPal calls only
runs.what: Authorize $230 with the sandbox test card + store_in_vault; a second $50 hold on the card's vault id (merchant-initiated); capture $200 of $230 (final); one Payouts batch (pro $140 + helper $40); partial refund $25; capture and batch detail; void the second hold.
runs.failedWhy: Reauthorize inside the 3-day honor period: 422 REAUTHORIZATION_TOO_SOON, as PayPal documents. The platform re-holds on the saved method instead when a reauthorize isn't possible.

runs.title: Multiparty probe (pro as payee, platform_fees)
runs.what: Orders AUTHORIZE with purchase_units[].payee = the pro and payment_instruction.platform_fees = 10%.
runs.failedWhy: 422 UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY UNSUPPORTED_PAYMENT_INSTRUCTION: needs PayPal Commerce Platform partner onboarding. Kept behind DONE_MULTIPARTY=1 with an automatic fallback; every hold records which flow ran.

runs.title: The whole app on the sandbox: 3 jobs
runs.what: Judges' tour (hire, change order bigger than the buffer -> re-hold on the vaulted card, evidence, checks, capture $230, Payouts); a dispute settled 60/40 (capture $185, partial refund $74, Payouts $99.90); hired then cancelled (void). Reconciliation: 3 matched, 1 pending, 1 unclaimed.

runs.title: The whole app again, plus disputes, a repeat visit and a checked invoice
runs.what: The three jobs again (the first attempt of this run hit 422 DUPLICATE_TRANSACTION: the capture’s invoice_id repeated across fresh in-memory states; fixed by making it unique per job, then rerun); escalation to PayPal Disputes recorded (sync: 0 disputes, a sandbox buyer opens them in PayPal); a repeat visit (DP-1004) held on the vaulted card; a pro’s off-platform invoice sent with PayPal Invoicing after staff review (no model serving, so photos went to a person). Reconciliation: 4 matched, 2 sent unclaimed, 1 pending.
runs.failedWhy: DP-1004, the repeat visit, was NOT paid after its checks: the rules checker failed 3 of 5 conditions (before, new_part, no_drip: the script’s photos were judged wrong) and sent it to review, and the script’s tour step then released it as the customer: $185.00 was captured and $166.50 sent to the pro over three failed checks. That was a bug in the product, not just the script: release did not require the failed conditions to be named. It was found again by the round-4 red team and fixed in round 4 (one capture guard: money moves only when every condition passed, or a person names the failures with acknowledgeFailed; confirm refuses failed checks), and the round-5 re-run below shows DP-1004 stopping in review, unpaid.
runs.correction: Corrected 2026-11-05 after Judge A’s review: this entry first said the repeat visit was “paid after its checks” and counted 7 of 7 passed. The raw file (e2e-2.json) shows the truth: decision review, three conditions failed, captured anyway.

runs.title: Milestone payments on one authorization (PayPal calls only)
runs.what: Authorize $600 (test card, vaulted); capture $200 then $150 with final_capture=false (authorization PARTIALLY_CAPTURED); refund $50 of the second capture only; a second $300 hold on the vaulted card, a $100 partial capture, then void the rest (VOIDED); final capture $180 on the first (CAPTURED, the rest released).
runs.failedWhy: Reauthorize of the partly captured hold: 422 REAUTHORIZATION_TOO_SOON (inside the honor period). The platform re-holds what is left on the saved method instead and voids the rest of the old hold.

runs.title: Milestones, retainage, a review window and a defect refund through the app
runs.what: A: a water heater in two milestones with 10% retainage: partial capture $594.00 for milestone 1, final capture $891.00 for milestone 2 ($297.00 of buffer released), every ledger balanced. B: a faucet with a 24-hour review window, captured $195.00 when it ended (no model was serving, so its photos went to review first and early pay could not be offered). C: a defect claim on retained money: the arbiter refunded the $17.55 retainage with a real PayPal refund on the capture.
runs.failedWhy: Every Payouts call (the two milestone batches, the retainage payout after the warranty window, the B and C pro payouts) was refused with 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: earlier runs drained the sandbox business account's balance. The server records each as failed and retries on its tick; the sandbox account needs funds added in the PayPal developer dashboard. Early pay was not exercised on the sandbox (covered by the mock tests).
runs.correction: Added 2026-11-05: this run’s file did not record the check verdicts, and the script then released every milestone that went to review without looking at them (before the round-4 capture guard existed). So this run shows the money path (partial captures, retainage, review window, refund), not that the checks passed. The round-5 re-run records each milestone’s verdicts and confirms only what passed.

runs.title: The whole app again with round-5 code (capture guard, PIN step-up)
runs.what: DP-1001, the judges’ tour: hired with the sandbox test card ($200 hold), a $47.05 change order bigger than the buffer re-held on the vaulted card ($247.05, old hold voided), evidence, every condition passed (before, new_part, no_drip, receipt, work_note: 5 of 5, rules checker; with no vision model answering, the photos went to a person), the customer released, captured $232.05 ($15.00 of buffer released, fee $23.21, pro $208.84). DP-1002: disputed and settled 60/40 by staff: captured $185.00, partial refund $74.00. DP-1003: hired and cancelled, the $200 hold voided. The PayPal dispute record waits in “requested” (sync: 0 disputes, there is no sandbox buyer to open one). DP-1004, the repeat visit on the vaulted card ($185 hold): its work note needed a fix, so it stayed in review and was NOT paid, which is the round-4 capture guard working where run 4 paid. A pro’s off-platform invoice was sent with PayPal Invoicing (SENT) after staff review. Reconciliation: 3 of 3 PayPal movements matched (2 captures, 1 refund). Earlier attempts the same evening are not counted: one before the PIN change (the same results, with the model labelling DP-1001’s checks), and a milestones run that timed out.
runs.failedWhy: Every Payouts call (DP-1001, DP-1002) was refused with 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: the sandbox business account has no balance left. The captures are real and recorded; the payouts are marked failed and retried on the server’s tick once the account is funded in the PayPal developer dashboard. DP-1004 is counted as not paid (its check needs a fix), as it should be.

runs.title: Milestones, retainage, a review window and a defect refund, with each milestone’s verdicts
runs.what: Each milestone’s check verdicts are now in the file, and the script confirms only milestones where every condition passed (before: it released whatever went to review). A: a 40-gallon water heater in two milestones with 10% retainage, $1,885.95 held: milestone 1 passed 3 of 3 (incl. its permit document) and was confirmed, partial capture $594.00; milestone 2 passed 4 of 4 (incl. the inspection), final capture $891.00, $400.95 of buffer released; $113.60 retained for the warranty window. B: a faucet with a 24-hour review window: 5 of 5 passed, confirmed by the customer, captured $195.00 (early pay wasn’t offered: the checks left it to a person, so there was no review window to pay early in). C: a faucet with 10% retainage: 5 of 5 passed, captured $195.00; a defect claim, and the arbiter refunded the $17.55 retainage with a real PayPal refund on the capture. Every ledger balanced. The checks were the rules (no vision model answered), so every photo condition went to a person, who confirmed.
runs.failedWhy: Every Payouts call (both milestone batches, the retainage payout after the warranty window, B and C) was refused with 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: the sandbox business account needs funds added in the PayPal developer dashboard. The server records each as failed and retries on its tick.

runs.title: The whole app, payouts landing: every batch SUCCESS
runs.what: After the sandbox business account was funded and a sandbox personal account was set as the demo pros’ payout address. DP-1001, the judges’ tour: $198.00 hold on the sandbox test card, a $47.05 change order re-held on the vaulted card ($228.55), the checks passed 3 of 3 and released the money by themselves (decision release, rules checker), captured $212.05, fee $21.21, Payouts batch NHJJNGLTHGWB2: the pro’s $190.84 item SUCCESS (transaction 8VF99473C3233221S). DP-1002: disputed, settled by staff: captured $165.00, refund $66.00, Payouts batch 8GGLLU6JVXYYC: $89.10 SUCCESS (29A826362H182824S). DP-1003: hired and cancelled, hold voided. DP-1004, the repeat visit: its third condition failed, so it stayed in review and nothing was captured (the capture guard). A pro’s invoice was sent with PayPal Invoicing. Reconciliation: 5 of 5 PayPal movements matched (2 captures, 1 refund, 2 payout items). Item statuses read back from the Payouts API: sandbox/payouts-1.json. Run with DONE_AI=rules: an attempt minutes earlier with the models on stopped at the tour because the evidence model failed the demo receipt as “the same image as one in another job” in a fresh, empty state (a false duplicate, reported to the model’s owner), so that run was not counted.
runs.failedWhy: DP-1004 is counted as not paid: one of its conditions failed, and it waits in review for a fix. That is the product working; the failed check is the demo pro’s evidence.

runs.title: Milestones, retainage, early pay and a defect refund, payouts landing
runs.what: A: a 40-gallon water heater in two milestones with 10% retainage ($1,885.95 held): each milestone passed its checks (permit, then inspection), partial capture $594.00 then final $891.00, $400.95 of buffer released; Payouts X6MR7FS9XJSQQ (pro $408.97 + helper $80.19) and YS9PWHNN2JATQ (pro $613.45 + helper $120.29), every item SUCCESS; after the 14-day warranty window the $113.60 retainage paid out in C5MRB9WEFH4LG, SUCCESS. B: a faucet with a 24-hour review window: the checks passed 3 of 3 and released, the pro took early pay ($163.17 in E6YD7V35DJB46, SUCCESS; fee $3.33), so the release had nothing left to send. C: a faucet with 10% retainage: 3 of 3 passed, captured $185.00, pro paid $149.85 in B5EFSV5PBNLWG (SUCCESS); a defect claim, and the arbiter refunded the $16.65 retainage with a real PayPal refund on the capture. Every ledger balanced. Item statuses and transaction ids: sandbox/payouts-1.json. Run with DONE_AI=rules (see run 9).

runs.title: The whole app with the models on: every check passed, payouts SUCCESS
runs.what: Models on (api/.env: Done-Audit and the photo model at 127.0.0.1:11471). DP-1001, the judges’ tour: the evidence checker labelled “model” passed all 5 conditions (before, new_part, no_drip, receipt, work_note). The decision was review, not an automatic release: the code leaves photo conditions to a person when the model is unsure. The customer then released: captured $232.05, Payouts batch UYBR5MJ2Y246G, the pro’s $208.84 item SUCCESS (transaction 9Y225274PC3151649). DP-1002: a dispute settled by staff, captured $185.00, refund $74.00, Payouts 28J5SXWPYVPKA $99.90 SUCCESS (54R45214D46197604). DP-1003: cancelled, hold voided. DP-1004, the repeat visit, checked by “model+vlm”: no_drip and work_note needed a fix, so it stayed in review, unpaid. Invoice sent. Reconciliation: 5 of 5 matched. Payout read-back: sandbox/payouts-2.json.
runs.failedWhy: DP-1004 not paid: two conditions needed a fix (the guard working).

runs.title: Models on again: the photo model turned down a BEFORE photo, so nothing was paid for the tour
runs.what: Same script, minutes later, models on. DP-1001: checker “model+vlm” (decided by code from the model verdicts). new_part and no_drip went to a person (“no photo description”, the photo model was busy), the receipt and the note passed on Done-Audit’s word, and the BEFORE photo was marked needs_fix: “shows it isn’t done yet”. For a BEFORE condition that is the wrong test: a before photo should show the problem. The tour stops at the capture guard, so nothing was captured for DP-1001; the job stays in review. DP-1002: settled, captured $185.00, Payouts PE6ZQSQBT73B6 $99.90 SUCCESS (8TL74951YA705925S). DP-1003: hold voided. An attempt between runs 11 and 12 (not counted) stopped the same way with four conditions turned down. Its DP-1002 payout (YWNNBQZEWZYW2) also ended SUCCESS. Reconciliation: 2 matched, 1 pending.
runs.failedWhy: DP-1001 not paid: the photo model judged the BEFORE photo as “not done” (reported to the model’s owner: before conditions must be judged as showing the problem). The model verdicts vary between runs on the same synthetic scenes; code refused to pay over them, as it should.

runs.title: Materials advance: a partial capture and a materials payout mid-job
runs.what: Models on. A 50-gallon water heater hired on the sandbox test card ($1,885.95 authorized for a $1,485.00 price). The pro asked for $87.03 of extra materials (a materials change order: a second expansion tank and a pressure-reducing valve); the customer approved. The pro sent the supplier’s invoice and a photo on site: the materials check read the invoice (done-ocr: HILL COUNTRY PLUMBING SUPPLY, $87.03) and passed, but asked for a person because the photo had no camera make (a drawn demo image); the customer approved with their PIN session. Partial capture 1TL5049225608972G of $87.03 on the authorization (final_capture=false), Payouts W32ZJXGD4KANW: the materials item SUCCESS (62T50885HG302110B). Milestone 1 passed 3/3 and was captured less the advance ($594.00); milestone 2 passed 4/4, final capture $879.73 with the parts in the price paid at the receipt’s total ($11.27 less than the $900 allowance), $325.19 of buffer released. Milestone 1 payout U88UPSFQX7X6Y SUCCESS; milestone 2 batch DNXWKYKVW73V8 still PROCESSING when read. Ledger balanced: captured $1,560.76 = $87.03 materials + fees + pro and helper shares.

runs.title: Venmo payout refused by the sandbox; a tip captured and paid out in full
runs.what: Payouts with recipient_type PHONE and recipient_wallet VENMO ($1.00 to a US mobile number) was refused: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR "Recipient wallet not supported in sandbox." So the stand-in refuses Venmo items the same way, and the platform sends a refused Venmo payout to the pro's verified PayPal instead, saying so (venmoFallback). A tip: its own Orders v2 order, intent CAPTURE, $5.00 on the sandbox test card, order 1KS10972UF1372944, captured at once (capture 3SW55366FF5947900, COMPLETED). The whole $5.00 went to the pro's sandbox PayPal in Payouts batch FSUBRBWBA9XF8 (PENDING, then PROCESSING with the item PENDING when read 12 s later). No platform fee on the tip.
runs.failedWhy: The Venmo payout: the sandbox does not support recipient_wallet VENMO. It is untested against PayPal; production behaviour is not verified.
